images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A compact graphite training console about the size of a hardback book sits centre frame on a pale neutral tabletop, its top machined with a single slot. A frosted acrylic cartridge with milky edges is slotted halfway in. Along the front edge runs a slim graphite progress rail with one acid-lime bead that has slid most of the way to the right end. Behind the console, a folded ivory card manual stands open like a small tent, its pages blank. To the left, a short graphite rack holds two spare cartridges upright, and to the right a closed ivory notebook lies squared to the edge. Fine dust sits in the slot, and the bead is nearly home. Everything is still and aligned. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same graphite training console now sits at the head of a long queue. Frosted acrylic policy cartridges line up behind it in a winding row across the tabletop, each pushed against the next, and new ones are frozen mid-slide down a graphite chute from the left rack, which has tipped over. The current cartridge has been ejected and flies up out of the slot, spinning. On the progress rail, the acid-lime bead has been flung back to the far left end, and a bright scuff shows its fast return. The tented ivory manual has collapsed flat under a falling cartridge, and more manuals fan open around it. Milky acrylic chips and dust scatter where cartridges collide, all traceable to the ejecting slot. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Folded manuals the size of barns have slumped into the hillsides. A dusty haze hangs over the distant ridges.
